name: legacy_eval_27
primary_text: Spent the weekend going through $LDO properly, here's the summary. The bull case: it's still the dominant liquid staking protocol by TVL, fees are real, the DAO has been shipping, and the dual-governance upgrade reduces the risk of a hostile vote. The staking ratio on Ethereum keeps creeping up, which grows the pie. The bear case: market share has been slipping for eighteen months as restaking and native options eat into it, the token has no direct fee capture yet, and a big chunk of supply sits with early investors who have sold into every rally. Regulators also keep circling liquid staking tokens and nobody knows how that ends. Valuation: on a price-to-fees basis it looks cheap here versus other DeFi blue chips, but 'cheap' with no value accrual has been a trap before. My honest take is that the token is a governance bet, not a cash-flow bet, and I don't have strong conviction either way. I'm not in it and I'm not getting in at these levels; I'll revisit if they actually turn on the fee switch. Not financial advice, just my notes, happy to be corrected in the replies.
